comment: Declared surfaces whose merge, in a repo where merging triggers automation on the
default branch, PERFORMS a real-world action rather than publishing code: it
provisions/mutates/destroys billable infrastructure, moves money, or is one-way.
Read by ai/bin/blast-radius, which is called by integration-gate before a merge.
Patterns are deliberately GENERIC (no product repo is named here). This file
lives in ~/dev/custom and classifies other repos by reading them, never by
requiring anything to be committed into them.
Adding a pattern only ever WIDENS what is held for the owner, which is always
safe. NEVER narrow or remove a pattern to make a merge pass
(ai/blocks/ops/safety-checks.md) -- excluding a path to go green is the named
forbidden move, and here it would silently restore the exact hole this exists to
close. If a pattern is genuinely wrong, the OWNER decides, and the change cites
the evidence.
Matching (ai/bin/blast-radius -> match?): fnmatch with FNM_PATHNAME, FNM_EXTGLOB
and FNM_DOTMATCH, so `*` and `**/` reach dot-prefixed files and directories
(gen_saas's .pkg/prod/tf read COLD without it -- DND-422). A leading `**/` also
matches at the repo root, and a trailing `/**` matches at ANY depth below.
HOLD (owner approval policy, 2026-09-28; ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> "Owner approval
policy"; Cody: "I want to shift to a \"don't require approval by default\"
strategy."). Each surface says whether its hit HOLDS the merge for the owner:
`always` (HOT whatever merging triggers), `on-merge-automation` (HOT only when
merging triggers automation -- the original rule and the default), or `never`
(reported on every run, never held). Only the owner's KEEP items hold: destroying
or replacing prod state (destructive-migration; infrastructure-as-code until a
plan verifier, DND-998, can tell a destroy or a cost change from a harmless
update), forge settings, loosening a quality bar, and the approval rules
themselves. deploy-automation became report-only by that decision. A `never`
surface must come LAST: a path goes to the first surface it matches.

surfaces.why: merging changes WHAT NEEDS THE OWNER'S APPROVAL (KEEP 6): the owner approval grant allowlist, the approval table, or the classifier and verifiers that enforce them, and the receipt chain a merge or push to main is accepted on (integration-gate and its shim, the receipt reader and seal, the merge and push guards and what they load, including the red-main content declaration ai/config/main-content-checks.json the merge guard reads its bar from (DND-1905) and the per-namespace GitLab bot identity map glab-athena pushes and writes as (ai/config/forge-identities.json and its reader ai/lib/forge-identity.sh with its jq programs, DND-1936), the merge role guard that keeps merging with the admiral, the forge identity guard hook and the agent PATH git, gh and glab wrappers that refuse a forge write or push not made as Athena with what they load and the session env that puts them on PATH, the forge auth guard that keeps the owner's forge credentials from agents, locked-merge, gh-athena and glab-athena, main-health and the critic verdict producer, and the declared merge gate ai/bin/harness-gate with the libraries it loads to discover its checks, read their bar from what landed or fail a check, and the tool scope table check-bin-help reads; athena:merge-boarding names each). No owner approval grant class covers this surface. The owner's verified click (--owner-approval click:<delivery_id>, ai/lib/owner_click.rb, which reads the owner's id through the private overlay resolver, held with it) clears it like any other hold: owner decision, Cody, 2026-10-02 (DND-1784), "Gate accepts a verified owner click, without hesitation."
merging changes the owner approval table (KEEP 6: changing the approval rules). Only the named SECTION holds; the rest of the file stays COLD.

comment: A hit when a named section's text differs between base and head, read from the
commits. A heading missing on either side, or present more than once, is a hit
(fails closed). Edits elsewhere in the file are not hits.

surfaces.why: merging changes forge settings or who must review (KEEP 4: forge settings or branch protection)
merging edits a check's suppression list, which is almost always a loosening (KEEP 5: loosening a quality bar). Removing an entry holds too: rare, and it fails wide.
known_gaps: A threshold in a config file (a coverage minimum in mix.exs, a .credo.exs check) and a check removed from a gate script are not path-visible; a landed-ratchet check is the honest mechanism (follow-up). Numeric harness budgets are already ratcheted against origin/main (check-agent-size).

surfaces.why: merging applies it: provisions, mutates or destroys real, billable cloud resources
surfaces.hold_why: KEEP 1 and 2 (destroy/replace, recurring cost). A path cannot tell a destroy or a cost change from a harmless update, so every IaC hit holds until DND-998's plan verifier can prove a plan does neither: a bar that cannot be measured fails.

surfaces.why: merging RUNS it: the migration executes on the deploy that merging triggers, and irreversibly destroys data. Ecto reversibility restores the SCHEMA, never the rows -- `remove :col, :type` in a `change` block is auto-reversible in Ecto's sense and every value in that column is still gone the moment it runs. NEVER use Ecto-reversibility to downgrade a hit here.

comment: This surface is CONTENT-gated: a path hit alone is NOT a surface hit.
Routine migrations (create table, add column, create index) touch these
paths on every feature MR and must stay COLD.
Measured 2026-09-20 over 364 migrations in gen_saas + walt_ui: a naive
verb rule (drop|remove anywhere) flags 59 and is ~50% precise on walt_ui,
gating `drop constraint` x15 and `drop index` x4, which lose no data.
This rule flags far fewer, and only where rows are actually destroyed.
Content is read from the file AT HEAD (git show <head>:<path>), never
from diff text: a diff hunk may not show the `def down` line, which
would make the up/down distinction undecidable. A file absent at head
was DELETED and does not execute on deploy -- not a hit, but PRINTED,
never silently skipped. Any other read failure is a hit (fail closed).

exclude_first.why: dropping an index or a constraint loses no rows; it is mechanically rebuildable by its inverse. This exclusion is what keeps routine schema hygiene ungated.

match_line.why: drops a table and every row in it
drops a column and every value in it
a `drop` whose argument this rule does not recognise -- the argument is what decides whether rows are lost, so an unrecognised argument is UNDECIDABLE and fails closed

match_region.why: raw destructive SQL in an `execute`. Scanned region-wide, not per-line, so heredocs are covered.

known_gaps: A lossy `modify` (narrowing a column type so Postgres truncates on cast) is NOT detected. Most `modify` calls are benign (null, default) and no pattern separates them, so this is a NAMED gap rather than a silent one; the captain's `Blast radius: IRREVERSIBLE` channel is its only cover.
A `drop table` on a table created earlier in the SAME migration is a hit, though it destroys nothing. Rare; fails closed by design.

surfaces.hold_why: KEEP 1: a destructive migration destroys prod data on the deploy merging triggers.

surfaces.why: merging changes what EVERY future merge does -- the machinery that performs the action

comment: DND-589 (the DND-422 class): the patterns above name the CI CONFIG files,
but merge-time CI also EXECUTES other repo files by relative path, and
those decide what a merge does just as much. Measured: gen_saas's
post-merge.yml runs .pkg/prod/bin/deploy-guard.sh (the guard that refuses
stale prod deploys) and ships .pkg/prod/docker-compose.production.yml;
walt_ui's .gitlab-ci.yml includes backend/.pkg/gitlab/terraform-aws.yml.
All read COLD, so editing them bypassed the owner stop.
`.github/actions/**` and `**/action.y{a,}ml` are static: a local action is
deploy-automation wherever it lives. This key adds the DYNAMIC part: every
file named by path, at head, in a merge-time CI config -- a GitHub workflow
with any trigger whose later runs execute the merged code (the same
workflow_trigger the automation term uses: every event except the
pre-merge ones, see PRE_MERGE_EVENTS) and every GitLab CI file (GitLab absence is not
provable) -- is a hit, and so is every file named by one of THOSE,
transitively. A `uses: ./dir` naming a local action pulls in its whole
directory (Dockerfile, entry point). Only paths that exist at head count,
so a word that merely looks like a path matches nothing.
A changed path ABSENT at head (deleted, or renamed away) cannot be named
at head, so the same walk also runs over BASE for it: a path merge-time CI
executed at base is a hit when the diff removes it (DND-793). Removing
deploy-guard.sh read COLD before that. The bounds below are the same on
both sides.
Bounds (each pinned by a self-test case, and each measured on walt_ui,
where the unbounded walk reached 372 files): only CI YAML, action
metadata and scripts are FOLLOWED (a data file a step reads is a hit, not
a source of further hits); YAML is read structurally, skipping subtrees
that select or cache files (`changes:`, `paths:`, `cache:` ...); script
comment lines are dropped; a bare name in a script resolves beside the
script, not at the repo root; `.md` is never a hit (documentation is not
executed). With them, gen_saas reads 45 files and walt_ui 61. (gen_saas read
12 until DND-590 made its workflow_dispatch ci.yml a root: that adds its CI
check scripts and, through paths those scripts name as data, mix.exs,
mix.lock and Dockerfile.)
known_gaps: Implicit build entry points are NOT followed: `make` reads Makefile, `mix`/`npm run` read mix.exs/package.json, `docker build .` reads Dockerfile, and none is named by path. They are the application's build definition, touched by every feature merge; gating them would gate every deploy. The captain's `Blast radius: IRREVERSIBLE` channel is their only cover.

A plain DIRECTORY named in CI (`cp -r .pkg/prod dest`, `cd apps/web`) is not expanded unless it holds an action.yml/action.yaml: expanding every named directory would gate every app change in a repo whose deploy `cd`s into the app.

A path an executed script names as DATA -- a grep pattern, an echo -- is a hit, since no lexical rule separates it from a path the script runs. This fails WIDE. Measured: walt_ui's backend/mix.lock is a hit because backend/bin/checks/self-test.sh greps CI for the string 'backend/mix.lock'.
A path built at runtime (a loop variable, string concatenation, an absolute runner path such as /home/runner/work/...) is not resolved.

The roots are a DENY-list of pre-merge triggers (pull_request, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment, merge_group), so a trigger that runs merged code (schedule, workflow_dispatch, release, pull_request_target, ...) or an unknown one is a root (DND-590). A workflow_dispatch run may be pointed at an unmerged ref by whoever dispatches it; that does not narrow the root, because the routine dispatch runs the default branch. A PR-CI workflow that also takes workflow_dispatch stays a root even when it is least-privilege (read-only token, no secrets, no environment, no id-token), and so does every file its scripts name (DND-822). The narrowing "dispatch + unfiltered pull_request + no privilege = pre-merge" was considered and rejected as not exact: a dispatch runs on the default branch's ref, and a run there can write the default branch's GitHub Actions cache scope, which a pull_request run cannot write and a push workflow restores from (gen_saas post-merge.yml builds the prod image with cache-from/cache-to type=gha). Nothing in the workflow file bounds that. The remedy for a repo that pays this cost is to drop workflow_dispatch from its PR-CI workflow, an owner-gated workflow edit; this manifest does not carve it out.

A name is counted as an execution (DND-865). Inside a shell script, telling `grep config/config.exs` from `source config/config.exs` needs data-flow through variables, functions, eval and implicit readers (`mix` evaluates config/*.exs without naming it), so no lexical rule is exact, and a name-only hit fails WIDE. Each reference hit prints its `root:` (the root workflow and the trigger that makes it merge-time), so the owner sees which trigger a name-only hit rests on.

surfaces.hold_why: Dropped by the owner 2026-09-28 ("non-security exit 4, deploy-workflow edits too"). Still walked and REPORTED on every run, so the owner sees what merging changed; never held.

comment: Candidates for the merge and push bar that do NOT enforce it, each with the reason (DND-1892).
The bar is the receipt chain, the merge role, and the identity a forge write or push runs as.
A control that refuses a push for another reason (a content leak scan) is not the bar.
Not read by the classifier. `blast-radius --self-test` computes the candidates; the rule is
defined once, in the DND-1892 enforcer-walk comment in that self-test, and is not restated
here. Each candidate must either hold in the owner-approval-policy class or appear here,
never both. Residual: the loaded-library scan reads one level of literal loads, so a
library loaded only through a variable set elsewhere is found by its name or not at all. A new
candidate fails the self-test until it is classified. An exclusion is a decision that the
file does not decide whether a merge or push is accepted, or as whom; this file is held, so
adding one needs the owner's record like any other change here.

excluded.ai/git-hooks/outbound-pre-push.sh: refuses a push by its CONTENT (the public-repo work-value leak scan); a leak control, not the merge or push bar: it does not decide which merge or push to main is accepted or as whom

It runs after the merge guard, may refuse a merge by its message, and swaps a file argument for its scanned copy; it never changes the sha, endpoint or method the merge guard judged
